result:
Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` runs 13 tests with 0 failures (`bunx guren check` also reports 0 failures — the three warnings about missing tests for other controllers are pre-existing).

I fixed the open redirect by adding `app/Support/SafeRedirect.ts`, whose `sanitizeRedirectTarget(value, fallback)` accepts only plain same-app paths: it strips control characters browsers would ignore inside a URL, rewrites backslashes the way browsers do, rejects anything that isn't a single-leading-slash path (absolute URLs with a scheme, `//host`, `/\host`, bare relative values, non-strings, blanks), and finally resolves the candidate against a probe origin to confirm it never leaves it — returning the fallback in every rejected case. `LoginController` (`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.ts`) now runs both the body's `redirect` and the `?redirect=` query value through that helper before `this.redirect(...)`, falling back to the unchanged default `/dashboard`, and `show()` sanitizes the value it passes into the Login page props so the hidden form field can't carry an off-site target forward; authentication logic itself is untouched, so a correct password still signs the user in (even when the redirect was discarded) and a wrong one still returns 422 with no session. Tests were added in `tests/SafeRedirect.test.ts` (unit coverage of the accepted/rejected shapes) and `tests/LoginController.test.ts` (end-to-end: `/posts/3/edit` is honoured, external/protocol-relative/backslash targets fall back to `/dashboard`, the Inertia props drop an off-site value, sign-in still succeeds after a rejected redirect, and a wrong password creates no session).
